subject: medieval fortress walls
title: The 5 Longest Sieges in History, Ranked (Leningrad Doesn't Make the List)

scenes.text: The five longest sieges in history. Leningrad lasted over two years. It doesn't come close.
Number five: Philadelphia, a Byzantine city in today's Turkey. Ottoman forces besieged it from 1378 to 1390: twelve years.
scenes.label: Philadelphia · 12 years

scenes.text: Number four: Gerdkuh, a mountain fortress in Iran. Besieged from 1253 to 1270: seventeen years.
scenes.label: Gerdkuh · 17 years

scenes.text: Number three: Candia, on Crete. The Ottomans besieged the Venetian city from 1648 to 1669: 21 years and four months, over 100,000 dead.
scenes.label: Candia · 21 years

scenes.text: Number two: Azotus, today's Ashdod. According to Herodotus, an Egyptian pharaoh besieged it for 29 years.
scenes.label: Azotus · 29 years

scenes.text: Number one: Ceuta. Moroccan forces besieged the Spanish city from 1694 to 1727: 33 years, the longest siege ever recorded.
scenes.label: Ceuta · 33 years

description:
The five longest sieges in recorded history, ranked by how many years they lasted.
Ceuta, held by Spain on the North African coast, was besieged by Moroccan forces from 1694 to 1727, about 33 years, the longest siege on record. Herodotus reports a 29-year Egyptian siege of Azotus (Ashdod). The Ottoman siege of Venetian Candia on Crete ran from 1648 to 1669, 21 years and four months, with more than 100,000 dead; the fortress of Gerdkuh in Iran held out from 1253 to 1270; and Byzantine Philadelphia in Asia Minor was besieged from 1378 to 1390. The siege of Leningrad, at a little over two years, does not make the list.
Which of these had you heard of? What should we rank next?
first_comment: Thirty-three years outside one city's walls. Which siege would you put at number one, and what should we rank next?
